findings.title: Exit code 4 silently repurposed from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means FEATURE_DISABLED. The update-compatibility tool is explicitly documented as 'fully scriptable' and its exit codes are the supported contract for CI/CD pipelines. Any automation written against the previous preview that branches on exit code 4 to decide that a recreate upgrade is required will now misinterpret that case: a 'recreate required' result returns 3 (which such a script would treat as an unknown error), and a 'feature disabled' result returns 4 (which it would treat as 'recreate required', potentially triggering an unnecessary full shutdown and downtime). The docs table is updated in this PR, but existing scripts get no warning. If this renumbering is intentional, it should at least be called out in the release notes/upgrading guide so adopters of the preview can update their pipelines.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path tested only for 'metadata' and documented exit code 4 never asserted
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only launches 'update-compatibility metadata' and asserts only the stderr message. The check subcommand's feature-disabled branch (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run) has no coverage, and neither test asserts the exit code, even though the documentation added in this PR advertises exit code 4 ('The feature rolling-updates is disabled') as part of the scripting contract. A regression where picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) returns the wrong code (e.g., 0 or 1) would silently break the automation contract this PR documents. Add a feature-disabled test for 'check' and assert exitCode() == 4 in both tests.

findings.title: Caution overstates requirement: operator only fails when an update strategy is configured without the feature
findings.body: The new CAUTION states 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' as a blanket statement. The PR's own UpgradeTest demonstrates otherwise: createInitialDeployment returns early without enabling the feature when no update strategy is set (updateStrategy == null), and that deployment is expected to become ready and to handle an image change with the default recreate behavior. The feature is only required when spec.update.strategy is configured on the Keycloak CR. As written, users who never set an update strategy will be told they must enable a preview feature to keep the Operator from failing, which is not true. Reword to scope the requirement, e.g. 'When spec.update.strategy is configured, the preview feature rolling-updates must be enabled; otherwise the Operator will fail to process the update.'
